items.title: Sixers Co-Owner Wants Philly's New Arena to Be Worth a Night Out
items.summary: Sixers co-owner David Adelman told FOS that Philadelphia's planned $1.5 billion arena, a 50-50 joint venture between Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment and Comcast Spectacor, should give people a full night out with something to do before, during and after a game or concert. He points to the Braves' Battery and the Patriots' Patriot Place as mixed-use models that also serve surrounding offices and the community. The South Philly arena will house the Sixers, the Flyers and the city's forthcoming WNBA team, which Adelman calls the first purpose-built building for three teams.
items.what_it_means: Owners are planning new arenas around the whole evening out, with the event as one part of it.

items.title: 5 Things We Heard at NWSL Championship Week
items.summary: At NWSL Championship week in Washington, D.C., league and team executives kept returning to stadiums after semifinal scheduling problems largely caused by teams not owning their venues, with the venue-owning Kansas City Current going on to win the title. North Carolina Courage chief business officer Ralph Vuono said tenants do not own most commercial rights, while owners keep concessions, ticketing, parking, merchandise and naming rights in full. Denver Summit FC president Jen Millet said lacking those revenue streams holds back team valuations, and commissioner Jessica Berman said the league is focused on infrastructure it can control or influence.
items.what_it_means: In women's sport, control of the venue is being framed as control of the commercial rights that drive valuations.

items.title: From investment to impact: Lessons from North American sponsorship leaders
items.summary: The Sponsor's roundtables in Toronto and Chicago brought together sponsors including BMO, Bell, Interac, KPMG, Deloitte and Abbott to discuss sponsorship effectiveness. BMO described using decades of soccer investment to engage around a major tournament without being an official sponsor, a difference between buying an association and building one. Sponsors also raised frustration with territorial restrictions on team deals, which clash with social media's lack of borders, and said league-wide deals can bring wastage in markets where a brand has no presence or a competitor holds the local team.
items.what_it_means: Sponsors are questioning how much territorial rights are worth when the audience they reach is not bound by geography.

items.title: Promoter Peachtree Entertainment Abruptly Ceases Operations
items.summary: Nashville-based independent promoter Peachtree Entertainment has told agencies and staff it is winding down immediately, after rapid expansion into venues and festivals including Rock The South and Rock The Country. A statement to local media said the company sustained more than $20 million in festival-related losses over the past two years. Pollstar notes Rock The Country faced political backlash this year, with artists pulling out and a stop cancelled, and that Peachtree had not publicly confirmed the news.
items.what_it_means: Festival losses can sink an independent promoter quickly, leaving host cities and venues to pick up the calendar.

items.title: Content, everywhere, all the time: Five sports video consumption trends to watch in 2027
items.summary: Using viewing data from the Canal+-owned Dailymotion network, SportsPro sets out five sports video trends for 2027. Dailymotion's Jennifer Matteucci says live remains the premium anchor, but the fastest growth is in clips, highlights, creator commentary and replays around the event. Mobile leads before live events and around social, connected TV leads for live matches and full replays, and desktop for news and analysis, so the same fan moves across screens through one journey.
items.what_it_means: Rights holders are being urged to treat the whole viewing journey around a live event as one connected product.

items.title: For some brands, humor plus niche targeting is a winning formula
items.summary: At the Brands&Culture conference, Columbia Sportswear's Matt Sutton and goodwipes' Meredith Diehn described pairing humour with niche communities. Columbia's Cannes-winning 'Expedition Impossible' stunt challenged flat-earthers and drew 10 million organic views, and a fax-in Helvetia fleece giveaway sold out online in 15 minutes. Goodwipes, which activates heavily in running, flew a 'Please take a pre-race poop' banner over the TCS New York City Marathon start village.
items.what_it_means: Brands are using humour aimed at tight communities, including at live events, to create wider conversation.

items.title: Megaforce looks to unlock Latam stadium stock for superstars' staging
items.summary: German staging firm Megaforce told IQ its Vega system, debuting in 2027, assembles the roof at stage level and raises it on its own towers, removing the need for cranes. CEO Michael Brombacher says more than 70% of Latin American stadiums do not allow crane access, which has forced some international tours to use smaller setups. The company plans to base the system in the region for half of each year.
items.what_it_means: Venue limitations shape which tours and productions fans in a region actually get to see.

items.title: Belmont Park's total makeover nears its photo finish
items.summary: SBJ toured the remade Belmont Park, a $555 million project with $455 million from New York state, which replaced the old grandstand with a building a third of the size. More than 10 new spaces are self-sufficient for event hosting, making year-round use easier, and the fourth floor will have 32 enclosed private suites. The building will host the 2027 Belmont Stakes and next October's Breeders' Cup.
items.what_it_means: A historic venue has been rebuilt smaller and more premium, with year-round events in mind.
